1. Recognize that you have a problem.

  2. Evaluate how problematic your problem is. Calculate your BMI and compare that to the minimum healthy BMI for your height. Make that your long term goal.

  3. Calculate how many calories you need to eat to reach your goal weight (it's the lose 1 lb per week number -- gotta take it slow to keep the weight off efficiently over time).

  4. Download My Fitness Pal from the app store. Use it to count calories without changing your diet. Count EVERYTHING, including the sugar and cream you add to your coffee, the snickers from after lunch, and the wine after work. You will be surprised how little things add up. You'll also learn what types of foods have the least and most calories.
    Do this for 3-4 days and see where you can cut calories easily.

  5. Now change your diet in two key ways. The first is by quitting certain foods completely -- I recommend cold turkey! And don't make excuses to finish what you have left at home. Throw it all in the trash. The things you must cut out immediately:
          * Any drinks outside of water, milk, and sugarless tea/coffee. This includes beer, wine, gatorade, juice, and soda.
          * Any snacks made with refined sugar: Chocolates, candies, cookies, baked goods.
          * Most processed snacks (like chips). Look for snacks lower in calories & higher in fiber/protein (e.g., pretzels, wheat thins, nuts, seeds...)

  6. The second key way is by reducing your sugar intake and increasing your intake of fiber/protein. Both fiber and protein increase satiety -- that is, they make you feel fuller. You will automatically consumer fewer calories by consuming higher quality calories.
    Looking back, I was eating what I thought were healthy foods -- pastas and veggies -- but I kept eating because I wasn't feeling full. I was missing the protein in my diet. I was consuming less filling calories, so I kept eating more until I felt sated. I ate less with higher protein/fat calories.

  7. Keep counting calories with My Fitness Pal. After some time, you will get a sense of how much food is enough and won't need the app so much. Took me a couple weeks, could take you more or less.

  8. To stave off cravings for sugary foods, have fruits and greek yogurts (high protein!) instead.

  9. Start working out. I HIGHLY recommend weight-lifting. Muscle burns more calories than fat. If you build muscle, your body will eat up more calories and that will help maximize the caloric deficiency and thus accelerate the weight loss process. This is also great if you're out of shape and cardio tires you out too quickly.

  10. Drink lots and lots of water. Sometimes we think we're hungry when we're just thirsty.

  11. Don't eat anything within four hours of bedtime.

  12. You can occasionally cheat with sugary snacks -- just calculate how many calories it'll cost and make the trade. E.g., I had terrible brownie cravings. So I would skip dinner and have me a brownie.

  13. More later. Additional advice and reflections from others is welcome.
